title: Mechanisms of alcohol's effects on prefrontal cortex circuits
text:
New treatments are desperately needed for the persistent symptoms of alcohol use disorder (AUD), including
changes in mood and problematic drinking. This proposal is designed to improve our understanding of how
acute alcohol and long-term drinking affect specific cells and molecules within prefrontal cortex neural circuits.
Our goal is to identify specific molecules that may comprise targets for the development of next-generation
medication treatments for AUD.

title: Investigating the role of reassortment, seasonality, and avian movement in H5N1 transmission and spillover risk
text:
Highly pathogenic H5N1 viruses have recently established in North American wild birds, posing an emerging
threat to human and animal health that requires new approaches for outbreak control. In this proposal, we will
reconstruct the ecological and evolutionary mechanisms that allow novel viruses to form in the wild bird
reservoir, spread through transmission and migratory movement, and spill over into mammals and agriculture.
Our findings will form a foundation for more effective surveillance, risk assessment, and vaccine strain
selection.

title: Team Science for MultiScale Data Mining and Functional Validation of Single-Cell Opioid Responses in the Context of HIV
text:
While population-scale SCORCH single-nuclei sequencing data enables the discovery of molecular alterations
resulting from chronic opioid exposure and/or HIV infection, the driving forces behind these changes and the
underlying regulatory mechanisms remain elusive. Understanding these factors is crucial for developing effective
therapeutic strategies. To address this gap, we propose the DMFV-SCORCH project to: 1) develop advanced
Artificial Intelligence (AI) methods for data mining on SCORCH and atlas-level public CNS single-nuclei
sequencing data, focusing on multi-scale dysregulations due to HIV/OUD, including regulatory alterations driven
by epigenetic, transcriptomic, network, and brain microenvironment interactions; and 2) conduct functional
validations using advanced genomic assays, such as epigenetic and transcriptomic manipulations via CRISPR
followed by snRNA-seq (e.g., CROP-seq) and high-throughput screenings using massively parallel reporter
assays (MPRA).

title: Natural language processing and machine learning for development of a Fontan Failure risk prediction model from electronic health records
text:
The Fontan operation significantly improves survival for infants with single ventricle heart defects yet survivors
face premature multi-organ circulatory failure and mortality. We propose to use natural language processing and
machine learning to automate anatomic and physiologic phenotyping of individuals with Fontan circulation to
develop clinically relevant risk assessment for Fontan failure across the age spectrum. This may lead to
development of technology to study other rare heterogenous disease states while utilizing fewer resources.

title: BRAIN CONNECTS: Photoemission Electron Microscopy for Connectomics
text:
In this proposal, we will develop and vet a new type of EM microscope for connectomics
with the potential to revolutionize how connectomes are made. This microscope will
democratize connectomes, making them cheaper and faster, and enabling full
connectomes of mouse brains, and with further optimization, non-human primate, and
human connectomes.

title: Correlating molecular behavioral phenotypes in a marmoset model of Huntingtons disease
text:
The marmoset is an increasingly attractive non-human primate (NHP) model for understanding neurophysiology
and there is a major interest in the field for using it to study neurodegenerative diseases, particularly to model
the social and cognitive deficits that accompany them, which current animal models are unable to do. At present,
no NHP models exist with trinucleotide repeat mutations at the endogenous allele as occurs in Huntington’s
disease, in part because of limitations in the ability of the CRISPR/Cas9 system to introduce long stretches of
DNA, as well as limitations in marmoset reproductive technologies. Therefore, we propose to establish a new
strategy that utilizes the expanded developmental potential of ground-state pluripotent cells to generate animals
that carry the precise human mutation through assistant reproductive technologies, which we believe will pave
the road for transgenic marmoset models as superior preclinical models to transgenic mice.

title: A Novel Immunological-Directed Biotherapy for Treating Rheumatoid Arthritis
text:
Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a progressive, chronic autoimmune disease characterized by inflammation and pain
of the joints that afflicts up to as much as 1% of the U.S. population1, 2. This project aims to develop a novel L.
lactis synthetic biology medicine programmed to express and deliver colonization factor antigen I (CFA/I) to
induce T regulatory cells for the treatment of RA. Successful commercialization would ultimately provide a
profound front-line medical advancement in the treatment of RA.

title: The role of maternal obesity in osteoarthritis
text:
Parental high-fat diets that are rich in omega-6 fatty acids have been shown to increase osteoarthritis severity
in adult mouse offspring. I hypothesize that maternal obesity programs offspring osteoarthritis risk by
epigenetically programming the cells of the developing knee joint. Here we propose that re-balancing the fatty
acid ratio in the presence of maternal obesity will improve pregnancy health and protect the offspring from
susceptibility to injury-induced osteoarthritis.

title: A Community Participatory School-Based Hydration Intervention
text: Drinking water instead of sugared beverages can help prevent obesity and dental caries, two of the most prevalent pediatric diseases. This investigation will partner with schools to conduct a water-promotion intervention, targeting multiple levels of influence on student hydration. Results will determine intervention effectiveness and sustainability, within a district that has newly installed hydration stations and is operating under a policy designed to enhance healthy hydration practices and promote water access and intake.

title: Development of broadly neutralizing human monoclonal antibodies against henipaviruses
text:
Henipaviruses (HNVs), such as Nipah and Hendra viruses, pose a serious global public health threat due to their
high case fatality rates and potential to cause pandemics. Our research aims to develop mAb candidates that
can provide broad protection against a wide range of HNVs. In the long term, this work could help enhance global
health by reducing illness and disability from HNV infections, contribute to pandemic preparedness, and provide
essential insights into the nature and behavior of these highly pathogenic viruses.

title: Improving Care Delivery for Individuals with Mental Illness and Cancer Across a Cancer Center Network.
text:
This research aims to improve treatment for cancer and serious mental illness and identify strategies to
increase the reach of person-centered collaborative care to community settings. This approach has potential
to mitigate a modifiable cause of premature cancer mortality and suffering for adults with serious mental
illness.

title: Street Experiences, Affect, and Coping: Harnessing Computational Models for the Development of a Cellphone-Based Intervention to Prevent Drug Use among Youth Experiencing Homelessness
text:
This project will examine linkages between proximal risk factors, affect regulation, and coping behavior, using
survey and ecological momentary assessment (EMA) data from youth experiencing homelessness (YEH). From
these data, this project will develop a data-driven app-based just-in-time personal support intervention (JIT-PSI)
that delivers responsive messaging to mitigate negative coping in favor of positive coping among YEH.
Leveraging growing number of public free WiFi hotspots and shrinking cellphone hardware costs, this project will
yield significant public health impacts by developing a sustainable, high-impact JIT behavioral intervention for
the prevention of drug use among YEH.

title: Towards Rational Discovery of Combination Therapies: LLM-Enhanced Gene Function Mapping to Explainable Drug Synergy Prediction
text:
The project aims to utilize advanced computational approaches to predict gene-gene and drug-drug
synergies, paving the way for advancements in precision medicine. By developing LLM-enhanced gene
function mapping methods and Bayesian frameworks for explainable drug synergy prediction, the team
will overcome current limitations in experimental methods and computational inefficiencies towards
rational discovery of combination therapies. Their multidisciplinary expertise in machine learning,
bioinformatics, and drug development will drive significant advancements in therapeutic target discovery,
combination therapy development, and the implementation of precision medicine strategies tailored to
individual patient profiles.

title: Expanding the capabilities and usage of the TELSAM protein crystallization chaperone
text: The proposed research is relevant to public health because it further develops new technology in protein crystallography and high-resolution structure determination. Development of such technology will accelerate the study of molecular disease mechanisms and development of more effective disease treatments. The proposed research is relevant to components of the NIH NIGMS’s mission that pertain to 1) increasing our understanding of biological processes, 2) laying the foundation for advances in disease diagnosis, treatment, and prevention, and 3) supporting the training of the next generation of scientists, enhancing the scientific workforce.

title: Novel technologies to detect disrupted RNA processing events in diabetic islets
text:
For this DP1 mechanism, we propose to use novel technologies to identify the RNA modifications and RNA
processing events that regulate functions in the pancreatic islet. We hypothesize that the post-transcriptional
editing of genes may be the important missing link for maintaining islet function in the context of T1D and T2D.
We will identify and characterize splicing events that are regulated by m6A RNA modifications in individual
pancreatic cells in rodent models of diabetes and assess the extent these modifications are conserved in
human islet cells.

title: Unmasking conditional dependencies of proteins influencing islet biology using machine learning
text:
A major challenge in complex trait biology is the difficulty in assessing the conditional dependence of individual
phenotypes driving disease traits, especially in metabolic diseases like diabetes. I will apply machine learning
(ML) methods, which can generate predictive models and extract these conditional dependencies, to 1) predict
islet function using islet protein abundances; 2) integrate the predicted influences of the proteins on islet
biology into existing systems genetics pipelines; and 3) determine the compartment-specific role and binding
partners of transketolase, an enzyme understudied in islet function which inhibits insulin secretion in mice and
humans. The ML field is relatively young and its application to metabolic disease has been limited, so these
studies collectively will provide much-needed methods for identifying conditional dependencies in diabetes
research that will extend beyond this specific application to other fields confronted with highly complex, multi-
dimensional data.

title: Chromosomal Rearengements in Aedes aegypti
text: The Aedes aegypti mosquito is the major vector of dengue and Zika fevers that threaten nearly half of the world’s human population. This project is aimed to characterize chromosomal rearrangements in the Ae. aegypti genome including their distribution across the global tropics, involvement in adaptations of the mosquitoes under different ecological variables and understanding the molecular basis of genetic divergence that underline inversion-associated phenotypes. This knowledge is critically important for implementing novel genome-based strategies for vector control.

title: Penn State - Natural Products Pharmacology Training Program (PS-NPPTP)
text:
With the growing interest in nutraceuticals, dietary supplements, and natural product-derived therapies, it is
critically important to better understand the pharmacology and toxicology of these entities. We propose to
establish a new PhD training program (the Penn State-Natural Products Pharmacology Training Program; PS-
NPPTP) to train the next generation of scientists needed to address these issues. The PS-NPPTP is designed
to rigorously train junior investigators – well-grounded in basic pharm/tox principles – who are facile with the
potential risks and benefits of ethnobotany and natural products pharmaceutics.

title: Reductive TCA metabolism in muscle stem cell aging
text:
The hallmarks of aging include stem cell exhaustion and related mitochondrial dysfunction. We have
uncovered a critical role for glutamine metabolism in the muscle stem cell through both oxidative and
reductive TCA pathways, which become dysfunctional with aging. Our evidence suggests restoration of the
glutamine pathway(s) rejuvenates aged stem cell function and improves myogenic capacity.

title: Modulation of Macrophage Polarization by Heterotrimeric G proteins: Implications of Gastrointestinal Inflammation
text:
Unresolved infections lead to chronic inflammation, e.g., inflammatory bowel diseases, and dysregulation of
microbial sensing and signaling in cells of the innate immune system, such as the macrophages, is a major
contributor to disease pathogenesis.
The overall goal of the planned studies is to decipher the role of the guanine nucleotide exchange modulator
GIV in the protective macrophage responses during infections, especially those that are geared towards
dampening of inflammation and efficient clearance of microbes, which must happen before the initiation of tissue
healing and the development of immunity.
Success by any measure is expected to not only reveal a hitherto unforeseen cooperativity between two distinct
cell signaling pathways in macrophages that appears critical for the resolution of infections, but also pinpoint
novel interfaces within the signaling cascades that enable such pathway crosstalk, that are lost in diseases, and
whose manipulation may serve as promising therapeutic strategy to combat chronic inflammatory diseases.
